title: The Hand of God
tagline: One goal illegal, one goal divine — the most famous 10 minutes in football history.

scenes.text: Villa Fiorito, Buenos Aires, 1960s. The slum children play football in the dirt with balls of rags. One boy never wants to stop — not when it gets dark, not when it rains. His name is Diego. The ball moves at his feet like it is alive.

scenes.speaker: Diego Maradona
scenes.text: When I had the ball, I felt free. In Villa Fiorito there was nothing — no money, no safety, no future. But with a football at my feet, I was the most powerful person on earth.

challenge.instruction: In Villa Fiorito the boys kick balls of rags — until Diego's cousin gives him a real leather football. Work out the size of the ball he will not let go of.
challenge.fact: For his third birthday Diego's cousin Beto gave him a leather football, and he slept hugging it. By the age of eight he was playing for Los Cebollitas, a youth side that went 136 games unbeaten.

scenes.text: Mexico City, June 22, 1986. Argentina vs. England. Four years after the Falklands War — two nations whose blood is still up. Fifty-one minutes into the game, Maradona punches the ball into the net with his left hand. The referee does not see it.

scenes.speaker: Diego Maradona
scenes.text: A little with the head of Maradona and a little with the hand of God. That is what I said — and I believed it. The English were angry. But the whole of Argentina wept with joy.

challenge.instruction: Mexico City, 22 June 1986: Argentina against England, four years after the Falklands. Beat the English goalkeeper and put Argentina through.
challenge.fact: Argentina beat England 2–1 in the quarter-final at the Estadio Azteca, then Belgium in the semi-final and West Germany in the final. Maradona, the captain, was named player of the tournament.

scenes.text: Four minutes later, Maradona receives the ball in his own half and runs. He beats one defender, then another, then another, then another, then another. Sixty meters. Six Englishmen. It was called the Goal of the Century — scored in the same match, four minutes after the most controversial goal in history.

challenge.instruction: Diego takes the ball in his own half and runs. Slide him through the English defence — Reid, Butcher, Fenwick, then Shilton in goal — and into the net.
challenge.fact: On Argentine radio, the commentator Víctor Hugo Morales wept as he called the run, crying 'Barrilete cósmico — from what planet did you come?' The phrase 'cosmic kite' stuck to Maradona for life.

scenes.speaker: Journalist
scenes.text: Diego — two goals in the same match. One by your hand, one by your feet. How do you explain it?

challenge.instruction: The journalist wants to know how he explains the first goal. Decode Diego's answer from the reporter's notebook.
challenge.fact: For nearly twenty years Maradona was coy about the handball. In 2005 he admitted on Argentine television that he had punched the ball in on purpose.

scenes.speaker: Diego Maradona
scenes.text: Football is the most beautiful injustice in the world. The ball does not care who you are or where you are from. I was a boy from the slums. And on that day, I was better than anyone on the planet. That is enough.

challenge.instruction: Six minutes from the end of the final, Burruchaga scores from Diego's pass. In the stands a furled banner is waiting — wind it on the right pole and read what Argentina is about to become.
challenge.fact: Argentina coach César Luis Menotti left Maradona out of the 1978 squad, saying he was too young to carry the pressure. Argentina won the tournament on home soil. Maradona said the exclusion 'broke my heart' — and that winning the 1986 World Cup finally healed the wound. In 1978, a 17-year-old sat out history; in 1986, a 25-year-old made it.

scenes.speaker: Diego Maradona
scenes.text: Jane Goodall and Peter Arnett are still in the rival's hand; they will come to the board one by one. Follow them, start the Lawsuit where they stand, and fight with Kill mode on. A player with no Great People left is out of the game.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 7 · Conquest. Deploy, move to wherever the rival stands, start the Lawsuit there, and attack with Kill mode on until the rival has no Great People left.
challenge.fact: With Kill mode on, a beaten card is discarded instead of returning to hand. A player with no Great People left, in hand or on the board, is out, and the last player standing wins. A kill won in a Great Person's own stat also counts towards their achievement.
